target_customer: System integrators, consultancies and professional services teams that implement enterprise software (Oracle, SAP, Salesforce, Atlassian ecosystems)
problem: Enterprise software implementations lose time and money in requirements gathering, documentation and project coordination.
business_model: B2B SaaS and agents for implementation partners (pricing not found)
product_category: AI agents for enterprise software implementation / professional services automation

founders.name: William Sun
education: Dropped out of Johns Hopkins (per launch post)
founders.background_notes: Launch post: four friends left jobs at Meta, Google, AWS and Apple; roles not assigned to individuals.

founders.name: Xinan Rahman
founders.background_notes: Named as a cofounder in the YC launch post; not a listed profile on the YC page (one profile says ex-Meta).

technical_complexity.rationale: LLM agents that capture requirements from calls and keep project documents in sync with enterprise systems; integration and accuracy are hard but standard for the AI-agent wave.

defensibility.rationale: Workflow embedding in integrators and partner ties (Workday, Microsoft, HubSpot investors) help, but foundation-model vendors and services firms could build similar tools.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No copy or acquisition found through 2026; the company only left stealth in April 2026.

market_need_then: Launch post: the team ran over 300 customer calls; named customer Valiantys (Atlassian's largest partner) calls Auctor core to how it operates (company site).

identity.mascot_or_character: 'Chief Bark Officer', a dog listed as a fifth cofounder in the YC launch post
identity.voice_and_tone: Playful founder-friend tone in the launch post ('four best friends')

brand_strength.rationale: Tiny, new brand with a playful launch-post touch but no press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Auctor is active and raised a $20M round led by Sequoia in April 2026 as it left stealth, about a year after the S25 batch, with strategic backers from Microsoft, Workday and HubSpot and a named integrator customer. Founders spoke to over 300 buyers before building, and the market of services firms adopting AI is hot. It is too early to know whether integrators will pay at scale or whether model vendors will absorb the wedge.
notes: Round confirmed by company site, TNW and IT Brief; dated April 2026 per eCommerceNews (the company page shows no date). Some aggregators call it a seed or combined seed and Series A; recorded as series_a because the company and TNW say Series A. A CodeConductor article cites about $500K raised, treated as outdated. Headcount varies (YC 30 on page, 15 in snippet, 36 elsewhere). No dated competitor source found for early 2025 (searches returned generic market coverage), list left empty. Name origin not found. Rahman's inclusion rests on the launch post.
